summary: Enterprise Suite AC-14 executable ERP/SAP parity composition map records all 23 SAP module rows as flat Oyatie service destinations with first-write owners, statuses, evidence refs, and explicit non-claims for ERP-suite microservice creation, durable business-document storage, Workflow execution, cloud deployment, and runtime audit-chain emission.

findings: The map is a typed immutable table plus validation helpers, avoiding a sprawling ERP service or duplicative runtime logic.
Validation focuses on invariants that can regress silently: required module coverage, no microservices/erp destinations, first-write owners, destinations, and no runtime/cloud claims.
Executable parity rows convert SAP comparison pressure into owned service destinations and operating-bar gaps that later cloud integration can sequence.
Capability flags keep deployed listener, durable document store, Workflow execution, cloud deployment, and runtime audit emission false until real slices attach infrastructure.

F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Tests fail if a SAP module row is missing, a forbidden microservices/erp destination appears, HCM/FI rows lose landed evidence refs, flat-service gaps are not represented, or capability flags overclaim runtime/cloud behavior.
findings: Positive full-map coverage and negative ERP-suite destination rejection are both covered.
Developers can call enterprise_suite_erp_parity_map(), find_erp_module(), capabilities(), and validate_erp_parity_map() without reading the full ADR table.
Focused parity-map tests/clippy, Enterprise Suite package-group tests/clippy, 24-package enterprise regression tests/clippy, fmt, data_class scan, and quality-marker scan passed.

alternatives_named: add executable parity map under Enterprise Suite composition
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: A typed map preserves ADR-0315 no-suite doctrine while making parity rows testable and ready for future cloud sequencing.
rejected_reasons: microservices/erp is explicitly forbidden by ADR-0315 and would create suite gravity.
Prose-only parity rows are easier to drift from landed HR/payroll/accounting evidence and cloud readiness non-claims.

findings: No secrets, customer data, network listener, auth bypass, or provider SDK are introduced.
The map strengthens security posture by refusing forbidden ERP-suite destinations and runtime/cloud overclaims.

F8_performance.regression_baseline: Static 23-row table validation only; no I/O or hot runtime path.

findings.summary: Validation is bounded over 23 rows and runs in tests/control-plane contexts only.

findings: Public fields carry data_class annotations and catalog row declares product-control plane metadata.
The map records production/runtime/cloud non-claims so ERP parity cannot be misrepresented as deployed capability.
The change is additive: one governance crate, catalog row, workspace membership, spec/tasks/evidence updates, and no external resources or migrations.
Rows include evidence_refs, first_write_owner, status, and capability flags for future review and cloud-integration sequencing.
Runtime audit-chain emission remains a non-claim; branch closeout uses static audit rows only.
Enterprise Suite AC-14 and D-11 record ERP parity as flat composition rather than a monolithic migration cliff.
SAP/Oracle/Workday/NetSuite import work remains future capability-specific slices referenced by row evidence/status, not runtime code here.

M1_challenge_assumption.premise_stated: ERP/SAP parity can be advanced by an executable composition map before durable/cloud runtime exists if the map explicitly rejects suite creation and overclaims.
M1_challenge_assumption.premise_evidence_ref: ADR-0315 module map, enterprise coverage matrix §3, and CS-ENT-SUITE-012 parity tests
M1_challenge_assumption.do_nothing_consequence: ERP parity would remain prose-only and could drift from landed HR/payroll/accounting evidence or accidentally invite a prohibited microservices/erp service.
M1_challenge_assumption.upstream_fix_rejection_reason: ADR-0315 and the coverage matrix are doctrine/reference; the missing seam is an executable local validation artifact, not a doctrine rewrite.

findings: This connects the landed HR/payroll/accounting Enterprise Suite foundations to the broader SAP parity roadmap while keeping future Oyatie cloud integration honest about remaining gaps.
Names use Enterprise Suite ERP/SAP parity map vocabulary and avoid creating an ERP service boundary.
Enterprise Suite spec, plan, todo, evidence, catalog, and audit-chain references were updated.
The crate is a control-plane governance composition artifact under Enterprise Suite; no microservices/erp path was created.
No listener, auth runtime, durable document store, provider SDK, Workflow engine/broker, child-service network client, cloud adapter, or runtime audit emitter was introduced.
No third-party dependencies were added; the crate has no external dependencies.
No wire API schema is changed; the map exposes typed Rust control-plane records only.
Validation deterministically scans static module rows for required codes, destinations, first-write owners, forbidden suite paths, and unsupported runtime/cloud claims.
